note: The assigned pair was checked against complete retrieved PDFs and complete relevant sections from six independent sources. Source conventions are compared, not imported. Every harvested result is assigned an item-level disposition; no source retrieval failed, no recovery search or drop was needed, and no empirical observation or statistical inference is used.

sources.title: A. I. Harte, Gravitational lensing beyond geometric optics: I. Formalism and observables, arXiv:1808.06203v2 (2018)
sources.locator: Complete 38-page PDF retrieved. §§3.1–3.3, equations (40)–(55), PDF pp. 10–13; Appendix A, equations (A.2)–(A.5), PDF pp. 33–34.

contents.name: §3.1, equation (40): source-free Maxwell potential equation in Lorenz gauge

source_review.read_extent: The complete paper PDF was retrieved and the full Lorenz-gauge potential equation and convention text were inspected.
source_review.supports: Confirms the curved potential-wave context; the local covector wave identity is separately proved with the imported curvature convention.

contents.name: §§3.2–3.3, equations (41)–(55): geometric-optics transport, gauge constraints, leading field and polarization

source_review.read_extent: The complete derivation around the ansatz, transport equations, leading field and polarization discussion was read.
source_review.supports: Provides the geometric-optics route and polarization comparison. The local result proves exact finite-epsilon identities under explicit constraints and does not infer series convergence.

contents.name: Appendix A, equations (A.2)–(A.5): residual of a truncated formal series and gauge-gradient term

source_review.read_extent: The complete Appendix A argument at equations (A.2)–(A.5) was inspected.
source_review.supports: Motivates keeping a finite residual explicit; the local proof differentiates its finite two-amplitude ansatz exactly and supplies its own component bounds.

sources.title: H. S. Reall, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision
sources.locator: Complete 125-page PDF retrieved. §6.2, equations (6.7)–(6.14), PDF pp. 61–64.

contents.name: §6.2, equations (6.7)–(6.10): curved-spacetime Maxwell equation and Lorentz force

source_review.read_extent: The entire §6.2 Maxwell and Lorentz-force development through equations (6.7)–(6.10) was inspected.
source_review.supports: Checks the covariant equation interface and Maxwell conventions. Reall uses Gaussian units; the local theorem specifies SI components and derives the weak/slow scaling itself.

contents.name: §6.2, equations (6.12)–(6.14): geometric-optics null-gradient ray calculation

source_review.read_extent: The scalar-wave calculation and its transition to Maxwell geometric optics were read through equation (6.14).
source_review.supports: Checks the null-ray conclusion and affine-parameter convention; the local proof establishes the one-form phase-gradient geodesic directly.

contents.name: §6.2 Maxwell field conventions in Gaussian units

source_review.read_extent: The field and unit convention around the displayed Maxwell equations was inspected.
source_review.supports: Used only as an independent check on the field equations; no Gaussian normalization is imported into the local SI component calculation.

sources.title: David Tong, General Relativity, University of Cambridge Part III Mathematical Tripos, Michaelmas 2019, complete author-hosted lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete 290-page PDF retrieved. §§4.5.3–4.5.4 and §4.5.7, PDF pp. 190–196 (printed pp. 183–189).

contents.name: §4.5.3, equation (4.52): Maxwell stress tensor and flat-frame energy density

source_review.read_extent: The complete metric-variation paragraph, displayed Maxwell tensor and adjacent energy-density calculation were inspected.
source_review.supports: Independently checks the quadratic stress and positive field-energy interpretation. Tong sets c=1; the local SI identities are proved from the assigned matter conventions.

contents.name: §4.5.4, equations (4.53)–(4.55): perfect-fluid tensor and projections
contents.reason: This pair makes no perfect-fluid projection or fluid equation-of-state claim; it treats electromagnetic scaling, charged dust, and prescribed test motion only.

contents.name: §4.5.7, equations (4.60)–(4.62): energy-condition vocabulary and Maxwell/dust examples

source_review.read_extent: The full energy-condition definition and the Maxwell and dust checks on the relevant pages were inspected.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent check on the positive electromagnetic observer energy used to distinguish a test field from a vacuum flat Einstein solution.

contents.name: §1.4.1, equations (1.104)–(1.111): dust/current, Lorentz force and Maxwell stress conventions

source_review.read_extent: The complete dust/current, force and stress discussion around equations (1.104)–(1.111) was inspected.
source_review.supports: Checks the matter and force conventions and quadratic stress structure. Carroll uses c=1 and Gaussian units; no source normalization is imported.

contents.name: §4.1, equations (4.8)–(4.21): weak/static/slow metric comparison

source_review.read_extent: The full weak-field coordinate expansion and slow-particle discussion in §4.1 was inspected.
source_review.supports: Provides an independent comparison for the Newtonian potential limit. The local theorem adds explicit uniform remainder and field hypotheses and proves its finite-time estimate.

contents.name: §§4.3–4.5: stress-energy and Einstein-equation context

source_review.read_extent: The relevant stress-energy and Einstein-equation passages were inspected in the complete notes.
source_review.supports: Checks the fixed-metric residual context; all claims here are derived from the local SI tensor definition, not Carroll’s Gaussian conventions.

contents.name: §2, equations (1)–(7): selected static charged-dust Einstein–Maxwell family

source_review.read_extent: The complete paper and the full selected-system section, including its unit note, were read.
source_review.supports: Used as a specialized check that a selected coupled charged-dust family fixes its charge-to-mass ratio; no coupled solution or normalization is imported.

contents.name: §2, fixed charge-density relation in the selected family

source_review.read_extent: The relation between charge and mass densities and its surrounding assumptions were inspected.
source_review.supports: Supports the scope note that a special model may retain a fixed ratio; the local scaling proof explicitly avoids claiming a general coupled-family construction.
